newsitem.title: UK: Monsoons help India silver demand surge to record.
newsitem.headline: Monsoons help India silver demand surge to record.

text.p: Higher farm incomes in India last year after a good monsoon led to a surge in demand for silver jewellery to yet another record, an authoritative report said on Wednesday.
Indian silver bullion imports, the world's biggest, increased to 113.5 million ounces in 1996 from 81 million the year before.
Total purchases since 1990 added up to 520 million, the report by research group Gold Fields Mineral Services (GFMS) said.
"The surge in demand from India during the second half of 1996 represented the most dramatic increase in the world silver market last year," GFMS said in its World Silver Survey.
The increase was triggered mainly by a good harvest, particularly in the northern tribal belt, where heavyweight silver jewellery remains farmers' favourite investment tool.
Bigger government subsidies to farmers, higher yields and the better irrigation also helped to keep agricultural incomes rising.
And buyers were attracted by lower silver prices last year.
"For silver in 1996, it was thus the overlapping of the most favourable rainfall pattern with that of heavy silver consumption which produced the remarkable rise in demand," GFMS said.
Silverware demand also rose but its potential was hampered by high interest rates to keep inflation under control.
Fabrication, including use of scrap, rose to 129.6 million ounces from 98.7 million, mostly in jewellery and silverware, making India the second largest user after the United States.
At 35 million ounces, industrial applications of silver were the third biggest in the world after the United States and Japan.
GFMS said silver was central to the social, cultural and economic pattern of Indian life, but demand was price elastic.

From 1974 to 1985 with silver above $8 per ounce, against $4.85 now, India exported 311 million ounces. The flow reversed in the mid-1980s, then lower prices and rising prosperity after 1990 saw unprecedented imports.
The farm sector remains the mainspring of silver demand, mainly in jewellery. Industrial fabrication was limited to big cities.
